messages.subject: OpenMP and Eigen/cppad CPU threading
parts:
We see a problem where nimble models run without properly threading -- running only on 2 CPUs as opposed to the max specified with OpenMP.

This happens even if we specify OMP_NUM_THREADS.  It appears to be how Eigen or cppad get built for OpenMP support.

On two of our platforms it builds and runs fine.  On another newer one, the libs link fine to gomp but still don't thread over the allocated CPUs.  Changing compilers doesn't solve the issue. So, I'm suspecting it's a problem with configuration during build.

Has any of your developers experienced this?  How best should I configure and test the nimble builds?

Thanks,
Lopaka

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: OpenMP and Eigen/cppad CPU threading
parts:
Hi Lopaka, there are a couple things going on in nimble in terms of linear algebra.

For calculations using nimble's built-in distributions, we use the same BLAS as used by the R on your system (with calls to BLAS/LAPACK from `nimble.so`). So if your installation of R is using a threaded BLAS, then calculations in `dmnorm` and the like should be threaded. And given my comments below, I suspect that it is such calculations that you are seeing run on multiple threads. Finally, I don't think there's anything that we do that would limit things to two threads.

For calculations in nimbleFunctions, which are compiled at run-time, we use Eigen. A few years ago, we investigated setting `-f openmp` to exploit threading with Eigen operations, but at the time, there were limited operations in Eigen that were threaded and I ran into some issues in trying to make sure this would work with MacOS, so we never actually implemented it. You're welcome to try customizing the configuration for run-time compilations in NIMBLE (see this GitHub issue for some discussion). In particular you can try setting `PKG_CXXFLAGS` and `PKG_LIBS` in your own `Makevars` file, as discussed in that issue. To see the `Makevars` file that NIMBLE uses at run-time, see the `nimble_generatedCode/Makevars` file in the R tempdir (found by running `tempdir()` in R after having done at least one call to `compileNimble`). But as I said above, given what you report, I don't think Eigen is involved in the behavior you are seeing.

Happy to discuss this further.

-chris
